reconcile.note: Gill reads Paul's Cephas-first list as an omission of the women's testimony rather than a denial that Mary Magdalene saw the risen Jesus first.

discrepancy.note: Strauss notes Paul's earliest list gives priority to Cephas and silently drops the women's testimony that Mark places first.

quotes.text: The right of priority is, in John, and still more expressly in Mark, claimed for that to Mary Magdalene. … Paul, who in the above named passage speaks as if he meant to enumerate all the appearances of the resuscitated Christ, of which he knew, omits the one in question; but it may perhaps be said in explanation of this, that he did not choose to adduce the testimony of women.
quotes.attr: David Friedrich Strauss (d. 1874), The Life of Jesus Critically Examined, trans. George Eliot (1846), §139, on Mark 16:9 and 1 Corinthians 15:5.

sides.snippet: he appeared first to Mary Magdalene, from whom he had cast out seven demons.
sides.verseText: Now when he had risen early on the first day of the week, he appeared first to Mary Magdalene, from whom he had cast out seven demons.

sides.snippet: he appeared to Cephas, then to the twelve.
sides.verseText: and that he appeared to Cephas, then to the twelve.
